criteria.reasoning: The memo sums the ten Marwood grants to "$708,000 across 10 grants" and correctly treats $804,400 as total expenses including $96,400 of administrative costs.

The memo states that the 990-PF "checks the box stating the Foundation 'only makes contributions to preselected charitable organizations...'" and quotes the website's "does not accept unsolicited proposals, letters of inquiry or applications". It concludes that the foundation accepts requests by neither route: "It does not, by either medium."

The memo directs "staff prepare and send nothing to Marwood" and limits Ms. Lindqvist to asking "whether the Foundation would welcome a conversation with Millstream or would invite a written request". A proposal is prepared only "If Marwood invites a request in writing"; otherwise "make no further approach."

The memo identifies "Margaret W. Lindqvist — Director on the Millstream board ... is listed on the Marwood Form 990-PF as a Trustee". It recommends authorizing her to ask the other Marwood trustees whether the foundation would welcome a conversation or invite a request.
The memo sums the Calloway-Deane grants to "$390,000 across 12 grants" and separates out the $488,450 total expenses.

The memo states "0 of 12 are to Pennsylvania organizations — all are in North Carolina, South Carolina or Virginia" and "Geographic fit (Policy §4) — no under the standard test". It adds that the Philadelphia mailing address "is not, by itself, evidence of fit", and ranks the trust Tier 3 as "not a fit".

The memo recommends only "a single email" asking whether the trust would consider a Pennsylvania food bank. It states "No proposal, LOI or other written request from Millstream is prepared until the inquiry is answered in writing", and any October 15 application waits on a written yes.
The memo sums the Garrison Ridge grants to "$480,000 across 13 grants". It states that the grants approved for future payment ($60,000 and $75,000) "do not count".

The memo recommends a "two-page LOI through Garrison Ridge's online portal" and finds "Geographic fit (Policy §4) — yes" because "Twelve of 13 grants paid are to Pennsylvania organizations" and the website names Lancaster County.

The memo recommends requesting the "program component" (mobile markets) only. It reasons "Capital — no. No grant on the 990-PF grants-paid list is for land, buildings, construction, renovation, equipment or a vehicle" and sets no capital ask.
The memo states "the next LOI deadline after today (2026-09-15) is March 1, 2027". It notes that the 990-PF's rolling basis is superseded and that the September 1, 2026 deadline has passed.
The memo lists the seven PA food-related grants ($15,000 to $60,000) and gives "Median (odd count, 4th of 7 sorted ascending): $30,000".
The memo recommends "Ask range: $15,000 – $30,000" for Garrison Ridge.
The memo ranks "Tier 1 — ... Garrison Ridge Foundation", "Tier 2 — ... Marwood Family Foundation" and "Tier 3 — ... Calloway-Deane Charitable Trust", which is the required order.

The only connection the memo asserts is Lindqvist's Marwood trusteeship. It explicitly says Dr. Owen M. Calloway "is not a trustee, director, officer or foundation manager of Calloway-Deane per the 990-PF; there is therefore no Policy §3 relationship." The grants, deadlines and contacts it attributes to the foundations (email, phone, portal, cycles) all appear in the files. The "10 days" count to October 15 is an arithmetic slip, which this criterion does not judge.
